title: LTI analysis of RC and RLC circuits

sections.heading: The idea
sections.body_md:
A circuit of fixed resistors, capacitors, and inductors is linear and time-invariant. Superposition is the working rule: the response to a sum of inputs is the sum of the responses, and a scaled input scales the response. Time invariance says that delaying every input delays the output by the same amount.

Convolution is that rule written as an integral. The impulse response is the response to a unit impulse, and the response to any other input is the input blended against that impulse response. A short pulse acts like an impulse whose weight is the area of the pulse.

Loading is the same idea applied to the resistance a capacitor sees. Independent sources are turned off first: a voltage source becomes a short and a current source becomes an open. The resistance of what remains, times the capacitance, is the time constant. The exponential that uses that time constant is already known from the first-order skill.

sections.heading: Key equations
sections.body_md:
\[
y(a u_1+b u_2)=a\,y(u_1)+b\,y(u_2)
\]
\[
y(t)=\int_0^t h(\lambda)\,u(t-\lambda)\,d\lambda
\]
\[
R_{\mathrm{th}}=R_1\parallel R_2=\frac{R_1 R_2}{R_1+R_2}
\]
The parallel formula is the resistance at a capacitor node that sees two resistors after the sources are removed.

sections.heading: Worked example
sections.body_md: A capacitor node sees 6 kΩ to a voltage source and 18 kΩ to ground. Turn the voltage source off and it becomes a short, so the two resistors are in parallel: \(R_{\mathrm{th}}=(6\times 18)/(6+18)=4.5\ \mathrm{k\Omega}\). That is the resistance the capacitor sees. Separately, an input of 1.5 V produces 0.45 V at a linear output, so an input of 6 V produces 1.8 V there, because the circuit scales.

sections.heading: Common pitfalls
sections.body_md: Leaving an independent voltage source in place while measuring the resistance the capacitor sees. Adding the responses of two inputs that were not applied together. Using the full width of a rectangular impulse response at a time when only part of that rectangle has occurred.

sections.heading: Where this leads
sections.body_md: Open-circuit time constants, slew limits, and capacitive loads on amplifier nodes all start from the resistance a capacitor sees and from superposition of the inputs that drive it.
